evidence.text: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06335173 (ALTITUDE-AD, 542 enrolled, active not recruiting) lists primary completion October 2026. The company moved Q3 reporting up to 2026-10-26, against 2025-11-12 last year, and on the Q2 call said it plans to go quiet before the readout. So this release is the natural place to confirm that the last participant's 18-month visit is complete, or to narrow 'late 2026' to a month. The market's expectation is the unchanged 'late 2026' wording repeated as recently as 2026-10-22. Confirmation is a mild de-risking of timing, and a slip into 2027 would be a sharp negative, given runway 'into early 2027'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior prints were all reaffirmations of trial timing: -3.5 (2026-05-12), +1.6 (2026-08-12), -3.0 (2026-03-26), -11.3 (2025-08-12, when the topline was pushed from early to late 2026 per aggregator summaries). On a reaffirmation the name has mostly drifted lower; a slip cost double digits.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 'late 2026' guide is fully priced. The narrower point is whether an LPLV or month is given on Monday. The early report date (announced 2026-10-19) and the +20% five-day run-up suggest some traders are already positioning for a timing statement, so part of this is priced. If it were fully priced, the run-up would have to be read as anticipation of data, and the release is unlikely to carry data because database lock follows the last visit by weeks.
evidence.independence: Separate documents: the Q2 call summary (go quiet before readout; https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/acumen-pharmaceuticals-inc-abos-q2-230426972.html), the Oct 19 date notice (https://www.biopharmawatch.com/news/ABOS/acumen-pharmaceuticals-third-quarter-results-october-2026) and the CTAD release of 2026-10-22, which announces only baseline-characteristics posters for Nov 16-17 and repeats 'late 2026' (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ABOS/acumen-pharmaceuticals-to-present-preliminary-baseline-hp5vi1e4200r.html).

evidence.text: The Q2 10-Q puts cash at $110.2m on 2026-06-30. After that date the company paid JCR $9.25m (July 2026), and amortization began on the $31.6m term loan: $10.1m of principal is scheduled for 2026, monthly from July, so about $5m in Q3. The Q2 operating loss was $32.6m. That puts Q3-end cash at roughly $66-72m. The company has disclosed no ATM sales in 2026 ($50m ATM available), carries going-concern language, and has runway 'into early 2027', which would end about a quarter after a late-2026 readout. The expectation is that the runway is reaffirmed. A shortened runway, or ATM use at about $2, would be the negative.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Going-concern language first appeared in the 2026-03-26 10-K and the stock moved -3.0. The Q1 print (-3.5) and Q2 print (+1.6) carried the same flag. The market has looked through it so far.
evidence.why_not_priced: The pieces are in the 10-Q, so most of this is priced. What is not is the Q3-end number and whether the company keeps 'into early 2027' with about $70m against about $35m of quarterly outflow. A market that had priced a shortfall would trade below the roughly $70m cash level, and at about $147m market cap it does not.

The peer migration risk and BFST's own resolution guide point opposite ways, so this nets to a small negative with a wide band.

The asymmetry is that a missed resolution guide on a 1.26% NPL book is punished more than a hit is rewarded.
